ga-circulars.whatItIs: Regulatory changes from RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, EPFO and NPCI, plus the exact figures attached to government financial schemes. For this exam a 'circular' is never a legal text — it is a rule with a NUMBER attached, and the number is almost always the answer.
ga-circulars.coreMethod:
1. Understand what is actually being tested. Every regulatory item reduces to five fields: Who issued it | What changed | The old figure to the new figure | Effective date | Who it applies to. You are not reading circulars; you are harvesting numbers.
2. Maintain a LIMITS AND NUMBERS sheet that you rewrite from scratch every month — rewriting, not amending, because rewriting forces recall. It contains figures only: repo rate, SDF, MSF, bank rate, CRR, SLR; UPI transaction limits including UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay and the enhanced category limits for tax, IPO, capital markets, insurance and hospital or education payments; ATM free-transaction and interchange limits; NEFT, RTGS and IMPS limits and timings; the DICGC deposit insurance cover; priority sector lending targets, overall and the sub-targets, noting that they differ by bank type; MSME definition thresholds; KYC periodicity; and the minimum capital requirement for each category of bank licence.
3. Maintain SCHEME FACT CARDS. For every government financial scheme record six fields: launch year | nodal ministry | eligibility age range | premium or contribution | benefit amount | tenure. The schemes that recur are PMJDY, PMJJBY, PMSBY, Atal Pension Yojana, PMMY/MUDRA with its three tiers, Stand Up India, PM SVANidhi, PM Vishwakarma, PMEGP, PM-KISAN, PMFBY, Sukanya Samriddhi, Senior Citizen Savings Scheme, NPS, the Gold Monetisation Scheme, Sovereign Gold Bonds, Ayushman Bharat, Kisan Credit Card and PMAY. The exam asks the AGE LIMIT, the PREMIUM and the LAUNCH YEAR — precisely those three fields, over and over.
4. Maintain a REGULATOR MAP, because 'X is regulated by which body' is a guaranteed question: RBI regulates banks, NBFCs, payment and settlement systems, foreign exchange, monetary policy and currency. SEBI regulates securities markets, stock exchanges, mutual funds, alternative investment funds and runs the SCORES grievance portal. IRDAI regulates insurance. PFRDA regulates NPS and Atal Pension Yojana. NABARD handles rural and agricultural refinance and launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme. SIDBI handles MSMEs. DICGC provides deposit insurance. NPCI operates UPI, RuPay, IMPS, NACH, AePS, BBPS and FASTag.
5. Scan rbi.org.in Notifications and Press Releases once a week for ten minutes. You are not reading the circulars — you are reading the TITLES, and noting only those that contain a number, a limit or a deadline.
6. Put every scheduled MPC meeting date into your calendar. Rewrite the rate block of the numbers sheet the same evening the policy is announced. A rate learned in August may be wrong in December.
tricks: Rate-relationship shortcuts turn one memorised number into four answers, and they survive any policy change because the corridor structure holds even when the rates move: MSF sits 25 basis points above the repo rate, the Bank Rate moves with the MSF, and the SDF sits 25 basis points below the repo rate. Memorise the repo and derive the rest — but re-confirm the corridor width at the latest MPC, since the corridor itself can be redefined.

Numbers-only revision. On revision day, do not re-read a single explanation — cover the figure column and recall the figures. The explanation is never asked; the figure always is. This alone doubles the speed of your revision passes.

The social security trio must be learned SIDE BY SIDE, never separately, because they are the most-confused item in banking GA: PMJJBY is life cover for ages 18-50 with cover continuing to 55; PMSBY is accident cover for ages 18-70; Atal Pension Yojana is for ages 18-40. The premiums were revised in 2022 — verify the current premium figures from a 2026 source rather than an older PDF.
MUDRA tier names in order with their loan bands — Shishu, Kishore, Tarun — are asked in some form nearly every year. The names are in ascending order of loan size, which is the mnemonic.

'Which of these is NOT regulated by RBI' questions collapse in three seconds with the regulator map: mutual funds and stock exchanges are SEBI, insurance is IRDAI, pensions are PFRDA. Three eliminations, no recall required.

Drill acronym expansions as their own five-second question type, because they frequently ARE the whole question: PMJDY, PMJJBY, PMSBY, APY, PMMY, PMEGP, PMFBY, NACH, AePS, BBPS, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, CBDC, DICGC, SARFAESI, IBC, NPA, SMA, PCA, PSL, PSLC, MCLR, EBLR, CASA, CRAR, LCR, AIF, InvIT, REIT.
traps: Quoting a policy rate from a stale source. The MPC meets roughly every two months, and a rate that was right when you learned it can be wrong by exam day. Diary the MPC dates and rewrite the rate block after every single meeting — this is non-negotiable.

Confusing PMJJBY with PMSBY. Different cover type (life versus accident), different age bands, different premiums, different benefit amounts. This pair is the most-confused item in the entire financial awareness block and the paper knows it.
Confusing the fixed-rate reverse repo with the SDF. The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the liquidity corridor, and both names may appear as options.
Misreading the deposit insurance cover as per account rather than per depositor per bank. It covers principal plus interest, per depositor, per bank — the phrasing matters.

Assuming priority sector lending targets are uniform. The overall target and the sub-targets differ between commercial banks, regional rural banks, small finance banks and urban cooperative banks. If the stem names the bank type, the number changes.
Treating an RBI draft circular or discussion paper as a final rule. Draft, final and effective-date are three different stages and the paper quotes the final one.

Assuming a limit applies universally. UPI's per-transaction cap differs by use case — tax payments, IPO applications, capital markets, insurance premia and hospital or education payments carry enhanced limits, and the enhanced ones are what get asked.

For every question whose answer is a RUPEE FIGURE or a RATE, mark it clearly as VERIFY-BEFORE-TRUSTING, because those change and your training data may be stale. PART TWO: here is my banking and RBI register for the last six months [PASTE YOUR REGISTER HERE] — using ONLY those facts, generate 20 five-option MCQs on rule changes, revised limits, new portals and regulatory decisions. Provide both keys separately. Finally, give me a checklist of every rate, limit and scheme figure I should re-verify from rbi.org.in and pib.gov.in in the week before my exam.

ga-rbi.whatItIs: Single-fact recall about the RBI as an institution: founding dates, board and MPC composition, and which powers belong to RBI versus the Government.
ga-rbi.coreMethod:
1. Build ONE 'RBI ID card' and rewrite it from a blank page every third day until it takes under 100 seconds: RBI Act 1934; operations began 1 April 1935; nationalised 1 January 1949; recommended by the Hilton Young Commission (1926); HQ Kolkata, shifted to Mumbai 1937; first Governor Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor C.D. Deshmukh (3rd); current Governor Sanjay Malhotra (26th, from 11 Dec 2024); maximum 4 Deputy Governors; Central Board 21; 4 Local Boards (Mumbai/Kolkata/Chennai/New Delhi).
2. Store the Central Board as a sum you can rebuild, not a number to recall: 1 Governor + 4 DGs + 4 local-board directors + 10 nominated by GoI + 2 government officials = 21. Rebuilding takes 8 seconds and never decays.
3. Learn the MPC as a 3+3 formula: 3 from RBI (Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, the DG in charge of monetary policy, one officer nominated by the Central Board) + 3 external members appointed by the Central Government for 4 years, not eligible for re-appointment. Quorum 4. Governor has the casting vote on a tie. Statutorily meets at least 4 times a year; in practice 6 bi-monthly meetings.
4. Memorise the one division IBPS exploits most — RBI issues all notes of ₹2 and above under Section 22; the Government of India issues the ₹1 note and ALL coins, and RBI merely distributes them. The ₹1 note carries the Finance Secretary's signature, every other note the Governor's.
5. Keep a six-item section list, treated as labels not law: Sec 22 (sole right of note issue), Sec 24 (maximum denomination ₹10,000), Sec 26(2) (demonetisation power), Sec 42 (CRR), Sec 45ZA (Government sets the inflation target), Sec 45ZB (MPC constitution), Sec 49 (Bank Rate).
6. Write the eight functions as a checklist with one distinguishing phrase each so 'which is NOT a function of RBI' resolves in five seconds: monetary authority; sole note issuer; banker to Government (Centre mandatory, States by agreement); banker's bank and lender of last resort; regulator/supervisor of banks and NBFCs; forex manager under FEMA 1999; developmental role; payment-system regulator under the PSS Act 2007. NOT RBI: securities market, insurance, pensions, commodity derivatives.
7. Keep a six-line 'RBI family' block: DICGC (₹5 lakh cover), BRBNMPL (note printing, Mysuru and Salboni), ReBIT, IFTAS, RBIH (Bengaluru), CRPC Chandigarh for ombudsman complaints. NABARD and NHB are NOT RBI subsidiaries any more — 100% GoI-owned since 2019.
8. Add the current inflation-targeting fact: the 4% ±2% target was renewed by gazette notification on 25 March 2026 for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. This is fresh and therefore highly likely in a December 2026 paper.
tricks: Act year versus operations year is one rule covering many facts. 'Established under the ___ Act' takes the Act year (1934); 'commenced operations' takes 1935. The same rule answers SIDBI (Act 1989, started 1990), NHB (Act 1987, started 1988), EXIM (Act 1981, started 1982) and NSE (incorporated 1992, trading 1994).

Every 'which committee recommended X' question in this group is a name-pair drill: Hilton Young → RBI; Narasimham → banking-sector reform and RRBs; CRAFICARD / B. Sivaraman → NABARD; Nachiket Mor → small finance and payments banks; Urjit Patel → inflation targeting and the MPC. Answer by name, do not read the option text twice.
If an option states the Governor's term as a fixed 5 years, eliminate it. The statute says 'not exceeding five years' with eligibility for reappointment — hard numbers here are always planted.

Headquarters questions across the whole paper come from one city map, not one fact per institution: Mumbai (RBI, SEBI, NABARD, EXIM, NaBFID, NPCI), Hyderabad (IRDAI), New Delhi (PFRDA, NHB, IBBI), Lucknow (SIDBI), Gandhinagar (IFSCA), Bengaluru (RBIH). Learn the map once, answer six questions from it.

On any 'who decides' question, run the three-way split: MPC decides the repo rate; RBI decides CRR, SLR and OMOs; the Central Government sets the inflation target. Three owners, and the question is always asking which one.
traps: 'RBI issues all currency in India' reads true and is false — ₹1 notes and all coins are issued by the Government of India. IBPS phrases it as 'which of the following is issued by the Government and not the RBI?'
RBI is banker to the Central Government by statutory obligation but to State Governments only by agreement. 'Banker to all State Governments' is a planted error.
The inflation target is set by the Central Government in consultation with RBI under Section 45ZA — not by RBI and not by the MPC. The MPC only decides the rate needed to hit it.
The three external MPC members are appointed by the Central Government for 4 years without re-appointment. '3 years' and 'appointed by the RBI Board' are the two standard distractors.

The failure clause is inflation outside the 2–6% band for THREE consecutive quarters, and the consequence is a written report to the Central Government — not one quarter, not a penalty, not a resignation.
NABARD and NHB are repeatedly listed as RBI subsidiaries. They were until 2019 and are not now. Trust the year, not the textbook.
ga-rbi.timeTarget: 12–15 seconds per question. If the fact has not surfaced in 15 seconds it will not surface; mark for review and move.
ga-rbi.masteryCheck: You can write the full RBI card from a blank page in under 100 seconds — Act year, start date, nationalisation date, founding commission, both HQ cities with the shift year, first Governor, first Indian Governor, current Governor with serial number, DG count, Central Board total with its five-part breakdown, four Local Board cities, and the MPC's 3+3 composition with term length — and score 13/13 on three attempts a week apart.

ga-rates.topicName: Policy rates — repo, reverse repo, CRR, SLR, MSF, bank rate
ga-rates.whatItIs: The current value, governing law and directional effect of each RBI rate and reserve requirement. The single most reliably asked banking sub-topic.
ga-rates.coreMethod:
1. Never memorise four rates. Memorise ONE anchor and two arithmetic rules. Draw the LAF corridor as a vertical ladder every time: MSF at the top = repo + 25 bps; repo in the middle (the policy rate); SDF at the bottom = repo − 25 bps. Bank Rate is always equal to MSF. From repo = 5.25% you derive MSF 5.50%, Bank Rate 5.50%, SDF 5.00% in four seconds. Only the anchor changes at each MPC.
2. Split the topic permanently into two families and label every term before answering: RATES (repo, reverse repo, SDF, MSF, bank rate — % per annum, RBI lends or borrows) versus RESERVES (CRR, SLR — % of Net Demand and Time Liabilities, banks hold). Every question tests family membership first.
3. Learn each reserve by exactly three tags. CRR: cash, held WITH RBI, earns NO interest, Section 42 of the RBI Act 1934, no statutory floor or ceiling since 2006, currently 3.00%. SLR: liquid assets (cash + gold + approved securities), held BY THE BANK ITSELF, earns a return, Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949, statutory maximum 40%, currently 18.00%.
4. Memorise the direction sentence once and run it forwards or backwards for every effect question: 'Rate or reserve UP → liquidity DOWN → lending DOWN → inflation DOWN.' Never re-derive economics in the hall.
5. Add a collateral column, because that is the modern discriminator: repo — collateralised by G-secs; reverse repo — collateralised; SDF — NO collateral required (this is why it replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the corridor floor in April 2022); MSF — collateralised by SLR securities, and banks may dip below the SLR requirement by up to 2% of NDTL to use it.
6. Add a borrower column: repo and MSF — the bank borrows from RBI. Reverse repo and SDF — RBI absorbs from the bank.
7. Maintain a one-page Rate Sheet with four columns: rate name, today's value, previous value, date of change. Update it within 24 hours of every MPC decision. MPC meets bi-monthly (April, June, August, October, December, February), so the October 2026 and early-December 2026 decisions fall inside your Mains window and MUST be captured.
8. Learn the lending-benchmark chain as a three-step timeline, because it is asked as a separate question: Base Rate (2010) → MCLR (1 April 2016) → External Benchmark Lending Rate / repo-linked lending rate (1 October 2019, mandatory for floating-rate retail and MSME loans, reset at least once every three months).
tricks: Answer the whole corridor from one number. MSF = repo + 0.25, Bank Rate = MSF, SDF = repo − 0.25. Four facts stored as one, and it survives every rate cut.
If two options in a rate question are exactly 25 basis points apart and one of them equals the repo rate, do the corridor arithmetic rather than trying to recall the specific figure.
Bank Rate and MSF are the same number in current practice. If a question offers a Bank Rate that does not equal the MSF you already know, you can eliminate it without knowing the Bank Rate at all.
Reverse repo has been frozen at 3.35% since May 2020 and is functionally dormant. Candidates compute repo − 0.25 and get it wrong. Store 3.35% as a dead constant, deliberately unlinked from the repo.
One-word memory hook for the legal source: CRR sits in the RBI Act, SLR sits in the Banking Regulation Act. This single hook answers two entirely different question shapes.
'Which of the following earns the bank no interest?' is CRR, every time, in one second.
Answer all direction-of-effect questions FIRST in your sweep — they need no current number at all, so they are immune to a stale rate sheet.
traps: Since April 2022 the FLOOR of the LAF corridor is the SDF, not the reverse repo. Papers still print 'reverse repo' as an option for the floor. It is wrong.
CRR has had no statutory floor or ceiling since the 2006 RBI Act amendment. The old '3% to 15%' band is still printed in older books and appears as a distractor. SLR does have a ceiling: 40%.
CRR is maintained as a FORTNIGHTLY AVERAGE with a daily minimum of 90% of the requirement — not 100% every day. 'A bank must maintain the full CRR daily' is a planted false statement.
Both CRR and SLR are percentages of NDTL (Net Demand and Time Liabilities), not of total deposits and not of total assets.
The repo rate is an MPC decision. CRR and SLR are NOT — they are RBI liquidity tools decided outside the MPC. 'Which of the following is decided by the MPC?' uses CRR as the bait.

Bank Rate is defined under Section 49 as the rate at which RBI buys or rediscounts bills of exchange — it is not 'the overnight lending rate to banks', which is the repo/MSF. Definition-swap options are common.
MSF is 25 bps above repo only in the current 50-bps-wide corridor. During the pandemic the corridor was widened to 90 bps. If a question dates itself to 2020–21, the arithmetic differs.
ga-rates.timeTarget: 10 seconds for a definition or direction question; 15 seconds for a current-value question. Never spend 40 seconds hunting a number — either the Rate Sheet is in your head or it is not.
ga-rates.masteryCheck: Given only 'repo = X%', you write SDF, MSF and Bank Rate correctly in under 15 seconds. Separately, you fill a blank 7-row table (repo, reverse repo, SDF, MSF, bank rate, CRR, SLR) with current value + governing Act and section + who holds the money + whether it earns interest, with zero errors, on three consecutive attempts.

ga-banktypes.topicName: Types of banks — PSB, private, small finance, payments, RRB, cooperative
ga-banktypes.whatItIs: Classification questions — which category a named bank belongs to — plus the licensing parameters (capital, deposit caps, priority-sector targets, shareholding) that separate one category from another.
ga-banktypes.coreMethod:
1. Draw the structure as a TREE from blank paper weekly, never as a flat list. Scheduled banks (listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act 1934) split into Commercial and Cooperative. Commercial splits into Public Sector (12), Private (old and new), Foreign (~44), RRB (28), Small Finance (11) and Payments (6 licensed, 5 operating). Cooperative splits into Urban (UCBs) and Rural (short-term: StCB → DCCB → PACS; long-term: SCARDB → PCARDB). Almost every classification question is answered by locating a name on this tree.
2. Learn nationalisation as two dates, two thresholds and one merger: 19 July 1969 — 14 banks with deposits of ₹50 crore or more; 15 April 1980 — 6 banks with deposits of ₹200 crore or more; New Bank of India merged into PNB in 1993, taking 20 down to 19. The 2017–2020 mergers took 27 PSBs to 12 with effect from 1 April 2020.
3. Recite the 12 PSBs until they are automatic, because 'which of the following is NOT a public sector bank' is a recurring shape: SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank of India, Indian Bank, Bank of India, Central Bank of India, Indian Overseas Bank, UCO Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Punjab & Sind Bank.
4. Build a two-column SFB versus Payments Bank contrast sheet — IBPS asks the difference far more often than the definition. Both: guidelines November 2014, differentiated licences, Nachiket Mor Committee. SFB: minimum paid-up capital ₹200 crore; 75% of ANBC to the priority sector; at least 50% of the loan book in loans up to ₹25 lakh; 25% of branches in unbanked rural centres; may lend and accept all deposits; first to start — Capital Small Finance Bank, 24 April 2016. Payments Bank: minimum paid-up capital ₹100 crore; deposit ceiling ₹2 lakh per customer (raised from ₹1 lakh in April 2021); CANNOT lend and CANNOT issue credit cards, but CAN issue debit and ATM cards; must invest at least 75% of demand deposits in SLR-eligible G-secs of up to one-year maturity and may hold up to 25% with other scheduled commercial banks; first to start — Airtel Payments Bank, January 2017; India Post Payments Bank launched 1 September 2018.
5. RRBs as one date, one ratio, two supervisors: first RRB Prathama Bank, 2 October 1975 (Moradabad, sponsored by Syndicate Bank), on the recommendation of the Narasimham Working Group 1975; RRB Act 1976; shareholding Centre 50 : Sponsor Bank 35 : State Government 15; REGULATED by RBI, SUPERVISED by NABARD; now 28 after the fourth-phase 'One State One RRB' amalgamation reduced 43 to 28 with effect from 1 May 2025.
6. Cooperative banks reduce to the dual-control point, which is the only thing asked: banking functions regulated by RBI, incorporation and management by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (Central Registrar for multi-state). The Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act 2020 brought all UCBs under full RBI supervision. Ministry of Cooperation created July 2021.
7. Keep a short 'firsts' strip: Bank of Hindustan 1770 (first bank in India); Bank of Calcutta 1806; Allahabad Bank 1865 (oldest joint-stock bank, merged into Indian Bank 2020); Oudh Commercial Bank 1881 (first limited-liability Indian bank); PNB 1894 (first bank with purely Indian capital and management); Imperial Bank of India 1921 → SBI 1955 under the SBI Act 1955; Bank of India opened the first foreign branch (London, 1946); HSBC installed India's first ATM (1987).
tricks: Classification questions collapse to ONE test: can it lend? Payments banks cannot. Ask the lending question before reading the options and most sets resolve in five seconds.

The three capital thresholds are the most-confused numbers here. Store them as a rising ladder — Payments Bank ₹100 crore, Small Finance Bank ₹200 crore, new universal private bank ₹1,000 crore (RBI's 2016 on-tap guidelines). One ladder, three answers.
RRB shareholding is 50 : 35 : 15 with the sponsor bank in the middle. Candidates swap the State and the Sponsor. Anchor on the State Government having the SMALLEST share.
IDBI Bank has been categorised as a PRIVATE sector bank by RBI since January 2019, after LIC took a majority stake. It is the most-exploited wrong option in this entire topic.
Paytm Payments Bank's licence was cancelled, and AU Small Finance Bank has transitioned to a universal bank. Any option naming either as a current member of its old category is stale and wrong.
'Which bank sponsors which RRB' is unanswerable from memory and appears rarely. Skip it in under two seconds rather than searching.
traps: IDBI Bank is a private sector bank, not a public sector bank. It appears constantly in 'which of the following is a PSB' lists.
Payments banks cannot issue CREDIT cards but CAN issue debit and ATM cards. 'Payments banks cannot issue any cards' is a planted error.
The payments bank deposit ceiling is ₹2 lakh per individual customer, raised from ₹1 lakh in April 2021. Books printed before 2021 still print ₹1 lakh.
SFBs must lend 75% of ANBC to the priority sector, not the 40% that applies to universal banks. Reversing the 40/75 pair costs a mark every time this is asked.
RRBs are regulated by RBI but supervised by NABARD. Options that give NABARD the regulation role or RBI the supervision role are both wrong — the split IS the question.

'Scheduled bank' means listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act with paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh. It does not mean public sector and does not mean nationalised — private and foreign banks are scheduled too.
14 banks in 1969 and 6 in 1980. Under time pressure candidates reverse them. Anchor on the earlier event being the bigger one.

ga-devbanks.coreMethod:
1. Build one four-row table with six columns and drill it as a unit: Institution | Act year | Started operating | HQ | Committee behind it | Apex for. EXIM provides export credit and extends Lines of Credit to foreign governments on behalf of the Government of India; it is not a commercial bank and takes no public deposits. ga-budget.whatItIs: The Union Budget 2026-27 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026 — her ninth consecutive budget. Constitutionally it is the 'Annual Financial Statement' under Article 112. In IBPS Clerk Mains GA it is pure recall: a question gives you a figure or a name and five options, and you either have the number stored or you don't. There is no reasoning path. So this topic is a memorisation-engineering problem, not a study problem: your job is to compress about 25 facts into a card you can rewrite from blank paper in four minutes, and to attach each number to its year tag (BE 2026-27 vs RE 2025-26) so the distractor options can't catch you. The single most useful structural fact is that the three headline numbers are arithmetically linked — expenditure minus non-debt receipts equals borrowings equals the fiscal deficit — so forgetting one does not cost you the question.
ga-budget.coreMethod:
1. BUILD THE 'BUDGET AT A GLANCE' CARD (8 numbers, all Budget Estimates 2026-27): Total expenditure Rs 53,47,315 crore (~53.5 lakh cr), +7.7% over RE 2025-26. Receipts other than borrowings Rs 36,51,547 crore (~36.5 lakh cr), +7.2%. Borrowings Rs 16,95,768 crore, +8.8%. Revenue expenditure Rs 41,25,494 crore. Capital expenditure Rs 12,21,821 crore (up from Rs 11.2 lakh cr), of which capital outlay Rs 9,43,042 crore. Centre's net tax receipts ~Rs 28.7 lakh crore. Transfers to states Rs 26,20,769 crore (+12.2%), including tax devolution Rs 15,26,255 crore.

2. LEARN THE IDENTITY, NOT THREE SEPARATE NUMBERS: 53,47,315 − 36,51,547 = 16,95,768. Total expenditure − non-debt receipts = fiscal deficit = borrowings. Practise this subtraction twice; after that any one of the three can be reconstructed in 15 seconds if the other two are on the paper.

3. LEARN THE DEFICIT PERCENTAGES WITH YEAR TAGS ATTACHED: Fiscal deficit 4.3% of GDP (BE 2026-27), down from 4.4% of GDP (RE 2025-26). Revenue deficit 1.5% of GDP in both years. Outstanding central government liabilities 55.6% of GDP, with a stated aim of about 50% by March 2031. Nominal GDP growth assumed at 10% for 2026-27. Never store '4.3' alone — store '4.3 = twenty-six twenty-seven'.

4. LEARN THE MINISTRY ORDER (top four by allocation): Defence Rs 7,84,678 crore ≈ 15% of total expenditure (up 15.19% over BE 2025-26; defence capital outlay Rs 2,19,306 crore, +17.6% over RE), then Road Transport & Highways ≈ 6%, Railways ≈ 5%, Home Affairs ≈ 5%. Mnemonic order: Defence, Roads, Rail, Home — D-R-R-H.

5. LEARN THE COMMITTED-SPEND FACTS: Interest payments are about 26% of total expenditure and about 40% of revenue receipts (≈ Rs 14 lakh crore). Committed expenditure — salaries, pensions and interest — absorbs about 65.3% of revenue receipts.

6. LEARN THE TAX CARD AS ONE STRING: '4 – 12 – 12.75 – 0.75 – 0.60'. No change in income tax slabs for AY 2026-27. New regime: nil tax up to Rs 4 lakh; zero net tax up to Rs 12 lakh via the Section 87A rebate of Rs 60,000; standard deduction Rs 75,000 makes it Rs 12.75 lakh for salaried. Other Finance Bill items: MAT cut from 15% to 14%; STT raised on options 0.1%→0.15%, on options exercised 0.125%→0.15%, on futures 0.02%→0.05%; all share buybacks taxed as capital gains; TCS on education/medical remittances above Rs 10 lakh cut from 5% to 2%; IFSC unit tax holiday extended from 10 to 20 years.

7. LEARN SIX SCHEMES WITH THEIR NUMBER WELDED ON: VB-G RAM G (rural employment, replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, guarantees 125 days) Rs 95,692.31 crore, +42.8% over RE. SME Growth Fund Rs 10,000 crore. Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme raised from Rs 22,919 crore to Rs 40,000 crore. Biopharma SHAKTI Rs 10,000 crore over five years. Carbon capture, utilisation and storage Rs 20,000 crore over five years. City Economic Regions Rs 5,000 crore per region over five years. Also flag as name-only: Semiconductor Mission 2.0, Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

8. EXAM PROTOCOL: read the year tag in the stem first, then scan the five options for the figure that carries that tag. Worked example — 'Union Budget 2026-27 estimates total expenditure at Rs 53,47,315 crore and receipts other than borrowings at Rs 36,51,547 crore. Estimated borrowings are: (a) Rs 12,21,821 cr (b) Rs 15,26,255 cr (c) Rs 16,95,768 cr (d) Rs 18,45,220 cr (e) Rs 14,10,000 cr.' Subtract: 53,47,315 − 36,51,547 = 16,95,768, so (c). Note that (a) is capital expenditure and (b) is tax devolution — both real budget numbers planted as distractors, which is exactly why the card must be tagged.

9. MARK-ARITHMETIC, NOT GUESSWORK: GA carries 1.25 marks per question with a 0.3125 penalty. A blind pick among five is worth 0.2×1.25 − 0.8×0.3125 = 0, i.e. exactly nothing. Attempt only when you have eliminated at least one option on actual knowledge; otherwise leave it and bank the seconds for a question you know.
tricks: The subtraction identity turns three facts into one: 53,47,315 − 36,51,547 = 16,95,768. Store expenditure and receipts, and the fiscal deficit / borrowings figure is free — saves memorising a seven-digit number and gives you a self-check when two of the three appear as options.

Defence gives you two answers from one number: Rs 7,84,678 crore ÷ Rs 53,47,315 crore ≈ 15% of total expenditure, and it is about 2% of estimated GDP. Whether the stem asks 'share of budget' or 'share of GDP', one stored figure covers both.

The deficits are a descending pair, 4.4 → 4.3 (RE 2025-26 → BE 2026-27), while the revenue deficit is flat at 1.5 in both. 'Fiscal falls, revenue flat' is one sentence that answers four possible questions.

Derive the GDP denominator once so any '% of GDP' option can be sanity-checked: 16,95,768 ÷ 0.043 ≈ Rs 394 lakh crore implied nominal GDP for 2026-27. If an option implies a wildly different base, it is not the fiscal-deficit figure.

Compress the personal-tax block into the five-token string '4 – 12 – 12.75 – 0.75 – 0.60' (exemption limit, zero-tax ceiling, salaried zero-tax ceiling, standard deduction, 87A rebate — all in lakh). Reciting five tokens is faster than recalling five separate sentences under a 20-minute clock.
traps: 'Total receipts Rs 36.5 lakh crore' excludes borrowings. Receipts including borrowings equal total expenditure, Rs 53,47,315 crore. A stem saying 'total receipts including borrowings' flips the correct option from 36.5 to 53.5 lakh crore.

Defence has the highest allocation among ministries, but interest payments (≈26% of total spending, ≈Rs 14 lakh crore) are the largest single expenditure item. 'Largest ministry allocation' → Defence. 'Largest item of expenditure' → interest payments. Reading past that one word costs the mark.

4.4% is the revised estimate for 2025-26 and will sit right next to 4.3% in the options. If the stem says 'estimated for 2026-27' the answer is 4.3%; if it says 'revised estimate of 2025-26' it is 4.4%.

Zero tax up to Rs 12 lakh applies only under the new regime through the Rs 60,000 rebate under Section 87A. Under the old regime the 87A rebate is still Rs 12,500 for income up to Rs 5 lakh. And Rs 12.75 lakh applies only to salaried taxpayers, because it includes the Rs 75,000 standard deduction — a non-salaried option-setter will use Rs 12 lakh.
Article 112 is the Annual Financial Statement. Article 110 defines a Money Bill and Article 266 the Consolidated Fund. All three appear as options in the same question, and only 112 is 'the Budget'.

Three different capital numbers exist: capital expenditure Rs 12,21,821 crore, capital outlay Rs 9,43,042 crore, and effective capital expenditure about Rs 17.15 lakh crore. Treating them as synonyms guarantees a wrong pick when two are on the option list.

VB-G RAM G was not created by this Budget — it came from the 2025 Act and took effect from 1 July 2026, replacing MGNREGA and guaranteeing 125 days instead of 100. The Budget's role was the Rs 95,692.31 crore allocation. A question asking 'which Act replaced MGNREGA' is not a Budget question at all.

ga-survey.whatItIs: Two things bundled, because IBPS asks them together. First, the Economic Survey 2025-26 — the Finance Ministry's annual review of the economy, prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs under Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran, tabled in Parliament by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 29 January 2026, three days before the Budget. It is not a constitutional requirement and its projections do not bind the Budget. Second, the standing concepts the Survey's numbers sit on: how GDP is measured and by whom, the difference between nominal and real growth, how CPI and WPI differ, and India's flexible inflation targeting framework. The Survey questions decay after one exam cycle; the concept questions repeat every year. Learn them together and you cover both the dated and the durable half of the economy cluster.
ga-survey.coreMethod:
1. SURVEY IDENTITY CARD (5 facts, asked as often as the numbers): Economic Survey 2025-26, tabled 29 January 2026, in Parliament by FM Nirmala Sitharaman, prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, under CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran. Stated theme: 'Disciplined Swadeshi' for strategic resilience, moving towards strategic indispensability.

2. SURVEY NUMBER CARD (7 numbers): Real GDP growth projected at 6.8%–7.2% for 2026-27. GDP growth estimated at 7.4% for 2025-26, against 6.5% in 2024-25. Medium-term growth potential put at about 7%. Retail (CPI) inflation 1.7% for April–December of 2025-26, down from 4.6% in 2024-25 — the Survey's 'Goldilocks' framing of high growth with low inflation. Current account deficit 0.8% of GDP in H1 2025-26, improved from 1.3% a year earlier. FDI inflows about USD 81 billion in 2025, up 13%. Private final consumption expenditure at 61.5% of GDP, the highest share since 2011-12. Foreign exchange reserves as on 16 January 2026 covered about 11 months of imports and 94% of external debt.

3. LEARN THE SUPERSESSION, BECAUSE IT IS A LIKELY QUESTION: on 27 February 2026 MoSPI released the new GDP series with base year 2022-23, replacing 2011-12. Under the new series, real GDP growth for 2025-26 is 7.6% and nominal growth 8.6%. So two different official growth numbers for the same year now exist — 7.4% (Economic Survey estimate) and 7.6% (new-series estimate). Store both, each with its source label. Base years also moved for CPI (to 2023-24, released February 2026) and IIP (to 2022-23, released around May 2026).

4. GDP CONCEPT BLOCK (six one-liners): GDP by expenditure = C + I + G + (X − M). GDP = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies. GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad. NNP = GNP − depreciation. Per capita income = net national income ÷ population. GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100. Producer of the data: the National Statistics Office under MoSPI.

5. DRILL THE ONE CALCULATION THEY ACTUALLY ASK. Worked example A: if nominal GDP is Rs 330 lakh crore and real GDP is Rs 300 lakh crore, the GDP deflator = (330 ÷ 300) × 100 = 110. Worked example B: with nominal growth 8.6% and real growth 7.6%, implied deflator inflation = (1.086 ÷ 1.076) − 1 = 0.0093, i.e. about 0.9%. Note what this tells you: nominal growth barely exceeding real growth is the arithmetic signature of very low inflation, which is exactly the Survey's 1.7% story. Two examples, both resolve, and both take under 20 seconds with the fraction written down.

6. INFLATION MEASUREMENT BLOCK: CPI is compiled and released monthly by the NSO under MoSPI (base year now 2023-24) and covers goods and services at retail level; it is the target variable for monetary policy. WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (base 2011-12) and contains no services at all. CPI headline includes food and fuel; core inflation is the measure excluding food and fuel.

7. MONETARY POLICY BLOCK (current as of August 2026 — re-verify in the last week before the exam): the flexible inflation targeting target is 4% CPI with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%, notified again by the Ministry of Finance under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934, for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 — the second such renewal since 2021. The Monetary Policy Committee has six members, three from the RBI and three external, chaired by the RBI Governor (Sanjay Malhotra) who holds a casting vote in a tie. Rates: repo 5.25%, standing deposit facility 5.00%, marginal standing facility and Bank Rate 5.50%, CRR 3.00%, SLR 18%. Cumulative repo cuts since February 2025 total 125 basis points. In its June 2026 review the RBI held the repo rate, cut its 2026-27 GDP forecast to 6.6% and raised its CPI forecast to 5.1%.

8. EXAM PROTOCOL: identify the source named in the stem before you answer. 'According to the Economic Survey 2025-26' and 'as per the latest MoSPI series' and 'as projected by the RBI' point to three different numbers for growth in overlapping years. Read the attribution phrase, then answer. If no source is named and two of your stored numbers fit, that is a genuine reason to leave it — a blind pick among five options is worth exactly zero marks after the penalty.
tricks: Store growth numbers as source-tagged pairs, never bare: 'Survey 7.4 / new-series 7.6' for 2025-26, and 'Survey 6.8–7.2 / RBI 6.6' for 2026-27. The stem's attribution phrase then selects the answer in about three seconds instead of triggering a fifteen-second internal argument.

The number 5.5 is a decoy that used to be the repo rate in August 2025 and is now the MSF and Bank Rate. Learn the rate ladder as a shape — SDF 5.00 below repo 5.25 below MSF/Bank Rate 5.50 — so the corridor structure regenerates all three even if one slips.

Nominal minus real growth gives you inflation in the economy at a glance: 8.6 − 7.6 ≈ 1 percentage point of deflator inflation, which corroborates the Survey's 1.7% CPI story. This lets you cross-check a suspicious option instead of recalling it cold.

Bundle the base-year revisions as one asymmetric line: 'GDP 2022-23, IIP 2022-23, CPI 2023-24 — two match, one doesn't.' Encoding the exception explicitly is what stops you from over-generalising when the CPI version is asked.

Fix inflation targeting as three separate askable numbers before you need them: target 4%, lower tolerance 2%, upper tolerance 6%, valid 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act 1934. Questions ask for the band, the target and the section number as three different items.
traps: The Survey is tabled by the Finance Minister but authored under the Chief Economic Adviser. Options routinely offer the RBI Governor, NITI Aayog and the Finance Secretary. Tabled by = FM; prepared by = DEA under CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran.

The Survey's 1.7% retail inflation figure is the April–December average for 2025-26, not the full-year figure and not the latest monthly print. A stem asking for the current month's CPI is a different question with a different answer, and by June 2026 the RBI was projecting 5.1% for 2026-27 — inflation had turned.

Two official growth numbers now exist for 2025-26: 7.4% (Economic Survey) and 7.6% (MoSPI new series with base 2022-23, released 27 February 2026). Answering 7.4% to a question that says 'as per the latest national accounts' is wrong, and vice versa.
The base year revision is not uniform: GDP and IIP moved to 2022-23 but CPI moved to 2023-24. Candidates who memorise '2022-23' as a blanket answer lose the CPI version of the question.

WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser under DPIIT in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry — not by the RBI and not by MoSPI — and it contains no services component at all. CPI is the NSO's, and it is the variable the inflation target applies to.

4% is the target; 2%–6% is the tolerance band. A question asking for 'the upper tolerance limit' is answered 6%, not 4%, and one asking for 'the inflation target' is answered 4%, not 'between 2 and 6 per cent'.
GDP is not GVA. GDP = GVA + product taxes − product subsidies, so growth rates for the two differ in the same year and both may appear as options in a single question.

ga-intl-org.topicName: IMF, World Bank, ADB, AIIB, WTO
ga-intl-org.whatItIs: Five multilateral institutions that between them supply a steady trickle of Mains GA questions in a very small number of fixed shapes: headquarters, head of the organisation, year of establishment, member count, flagship report, and India's standing inside the body. The content is finite and almost entirely static — but two of the five details changed recently enough that most study material is out of date: the AIIB got a new president on 16 January 2026 (Zou Jiayi, replacing founding president Jin Liqun) and the WTO held its 14th Ministerial Conference at Yaoundé, Cameroon in March 2026. This is a grid to be memorised column-by-column, not an economics topic to be understood. Built properly it is one of the highest-reliability blocks in GA, because the facts do not move much and the question shapes are fixed.
ga-intl-org.coreMethod:
1. BUILD A SIX-COLUMN GRID ON ONE SHEET — Organisation | Established / HQ | Head (name + nationality + start date) | Members | Flagship reports | India's position. Fill it once by hand from the official sites, then drill it vertically (all five HQs, then all five heads, then all five member counts). Vertical drilling matches how the exam asks; horizontal recitation does not.

2. IMF: conceived at the Bretton Woods Conference, July 1944; came into existence 27 December 1945; began financial operations 1 March 1947. HQ Washington DC. 191 members (Liechtenstein became the 191st on 21 October 2024). Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva of Bulgaria, second term from 1 October 2024. First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz, since 6 October 2025. Reports: World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report, Fiscal Monitor. Special Drawing Right created in 1969; the basket has five currencies — US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, pound sterling. India joined on 27 December 1945; quota SDR 13,114.4 million, about 2.75% share, the eighth-largest; India's Governor at the IMF is the Union Finance Minister and the RBI Governor is the Alternate Governor.

3. WORLD BANK GROUP: five institutions with five different membership counts — IBRD (1944, 189 members), IDA (1960, 175), IFC (1956, 186), MIGA (1988, 182), ICSID (1966, 158). HQ Washington DC. President Ajay Banga, an Indian-born American, took office 2 June 2023 for a five-year term. Reports: World Development Report, Global Economic Prospects (January and June), Business Ready or B-READY, which replaced the discontinued Doing Business report.

4. ADB: established 19 December 1966, HQ Manila, Philippines. 69 members, 49 of them from the Asia-Pacific region. President Masato Kanda of Japan, the 11th president, took office 24 February 2025 — by long convention the ADB president is Japanese. Largest shareholders: Japan and the United States tied at 15.6% each, then China 6.4%, India 6.3%, Australia 5.8%. India is a founding member and has been among its largest borrowers. Flagship report: Asian Development Outlook.

5. AIIB: proposed 2013, Articles of Agreement signed 2015, began operations 16 January 2016. HQ Beijing, China. 111 approved members (106 full members and 5 prospective). President Zou Jiayi of China took office on 16 January 2026 — the bank's tenth anniversary — for a five-year term, succeeding founding president Jin Liqun who served two five-year terms. China is the largest shareholder with about 26.5% of voting power; India is the second-largest at roughly 7.5%. In its first decade the bank approved close to USD 70 billion across 361 projects.

6. WTO: established 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement signed 15 April 1994, succeeding the GATT which had operated from 1948. HQ Geneva, Switzerland. 166 members. Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria, the first woman and first African to hold the post, reappointed for a second four-year term from 1 September 2025. Decisions are taken by consensus, one member one vote; the WTO does not lend money. The 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) was held 26–30 March 2026 at Yaoundé, Cameroon; MC13 was Abu Dhabi in February 2024. India is a founding WTO member and was a founding contracting party to GATT. Flagship report: World Trade Report.

7. DRILL BY COLUMN, THREE PASSES: pass one, cover everything but the organisation names and write the five HQs. Pass two, write the five heads with nationality and start date. Pass three, write the member counts in ascending order. Each pass should take under 60 seconds by the third day.

8. EXAM PROTOCOL: these questions are one-step lookups; the only real risk is answering a slightly different question from the one asked. Read whether the stem asks for the head's name or nationality, the year of establishment or the year of commencement of operations, and which institution of the World Bank Group is meant. If the grid does not contain the answer, leave it — a blind pick among five options nets exactly zero after the 0.25-per-mark penalty, so it costs you time for nothing.
tricks: Chain the member counts in one ascending sequence — ADB 69 < AIIB 111 < WTO 166 < IBRD 189 < IMF 191 — so a single ordered string answers five separate possible questions and instantly flags an implausible option.

Learn the headquarters as a 2-2-1 split: two in Washington DC (IMF, World Bank — the Bretton Woods twins), two in Asia (ADB in Manila, AIIB in Beijing), one in Europe (WTO in Geneva). Three chunks beat five isolated facts.

Store each head with a nationality tag, because nationality is asked as often as the name: Georgieva–Bulgaria, Banga–United States (born in India), Kanda–Japan, Zou Jiayi–China, Okonjo-Iweala–Nigeria. One extra token per head, and it covers a whole second family of questions.

Bind India's rank to each body in one line — IMF 8th-largest quota, ADB 4th-largest shareholder, AIIB 2nd-largest shareholder, WTO and GATT founding member. 'Eight, four, two, founder' is a four-token string that answers the most common India-specific stem.

Tag each report to exactly one owner so the matching questions are instant: World Economic Outlook and Fiscal Monitor to the IMF, World Development Report and Global Economic Prospects to the World Bank, Asian Development Outlook to the ADB, World Trade Report to the WTO.
traps: Anything printed before January 2026 names Jin Liqun as AIIB president. He completed two five-year terms and Zou Jiayi took over on 16 January 2026. Old capsules and older editions of GK books are wrong on this specific point.

'World Bank membership' has five possible correct answers depending on the institution: IBRD 189, IDA 175, IFC 186, MIGA 182, ICSID 158. Unqualified, the intended answer is IBRD's 189 — but if the stem names IDA or MIGA, 189 is wrong.

The IMF has 191 members and the IBRD 189. These are close enough that they get swapped under time pressure, and both will appear in the same option list. Liechtenstein joining on 21 October 2024 as the 191st member is the fact that fixes the IMF figure.

The WTO has three separate dates and options mix them freely: GATT began operating in 1948, the Marrakesh Agreement was signed 15 April 1994, and the WTO came into existence 1 January 1995. 'Established' means 1995.

The IMF also has three dates: Bretton Woods Conference July 1944, formal existence 27 December 1945, start of financial operations 1 March 1947. A stem saying 'commenced operations' does not want 1945.

Japan and the United States are joint-largest ADB shareholders at 15.6% each — answering 'Japan' alone to a 'largest shareholder' question is only right if the option list forces a single country; read whether the stem allows a tie or asks for 'the largest shareholders'.

The WTO settles disputes and sets trade rules but does not lend money. Options that describe it as providing balance-of-payments support are describing the IMF; options about long-term development finance are describing the World Bank or ADB.

For the IMF and World Bank, India's Governor is the Union Finance Minister and the RBI Governor is the Alternate Governor. Option lists reverse this pairing, and the RBI Governor is the intuitive-looking wrong answer.

ga-payments.topicName: Payment Systems — NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, AEPS
ga-payments.whatItIs: The five retail and wholesale money-movement rails used in India, and the rules that separate them. Examiners test three things: WHO operates each system (the Reserve Bank of India runs RTGS and NEFT; the National Payments Corporation of India runs IMPS, UPI, AEPS, NACH, RuPay, Bharat BillPay and FASTag), HOW each settles (real-time and one-by-one, or in timed batches), and WHAT the amount limits and identifiers are. This is a pure recall topic with no reasoning, which makes it fast marks in a 40-question, 20-minute General Awareness section — but the numbers change by circular, so what you memorise must be current. All figures below were verified in 2026 and should be re-checked in the fortnight before the Mains on 27 December 2026.
ga-payments.coreMethod:
1. LEARN THE OWNERSHIP SPLIT FIRST, because it is the most frequently asked single fact. RBI owns and operates RTGS and NEFT. NPCI operates IMPS, UPI, AEPS, NACH, RuPay, BBPS/Bharat BillPay, NETC FASTag and Cheque Truncation-related retail services. NPCI was incorporated in 2008 as a not-for-profit company promoted by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
2. LEARN THE SETTLEMENT MECHANISM, which the acronyms encode. RTGS = Real Time Gross Settlement: each instruction settles individually and immediately, with no netting. NEFT = National Electronic Funds Transfer: deferred NET settlement, so instructions are pooled and settled in batches — currently 48 half-hourly batches a day, at 00:00, 00:30, 01:00 and so on through 23:30. Both have been available 24x7x365: NEFT since 16 December 2019, RTGS since 14 December 2020.
3. LEARN THE LIMITS AS A LADDER OF PER-TRANSACTION CEILINGS, with RTGS deliberately placed outside it.
   - UPI Lite: Rs 1,000 per transaction; on-device wallet balance capped at Rs 5,000; no UPI PIN required for a payment.
   - AEPS: Rs 10,000 per transaction; NPCI also caps cumulative inward-plus-outward fund transfer at Rs 50,000 per account per month.
   - UPI 123Pay (feature phones, no internet): Rs 10,000 per transaction.
   - UPI (normal): Rs 1 lakh per transaction by default; up to Rs 5 lakh per transaction in specified categories such as capital markets, insurance, education and healthcare.
   - IMPS: Rs 5 lakh per transaction (raised from Rs 2 lakh in 2021).
   - RTGS: MINIMUM Rs 2 lakh per customer transaction, with NO maximum prescribed by the RBI. It is the only one of the five with a floor rather than a ceiling.
   - NEFT: no minimum and no maximum prescribed by the RBI; however, cash-based walk-in remittances are capped at Rs 50,000 per transaction.
   Banks may impose tighter limits than any of these.
4. LEARN THE IDENTIFIERS. NEFT and RTGS use the beneficiary's account number plus the 11-character IFSC. IMPS can use account number plus IFSC, OR mobile number plus MMID (a 7-digit Mobile Money Identifier). UPI uses a Virtual Payment Address (a UPI ID such as name@bank) or a mobile number or a QR code, and requires a UPI PIN. AEPS uses only the Aadhaar number, the bank's IIN, and a biometric (fingerprint or iris) — no card, no PIN, no signature, no cheque.
5. LEARN AEPS AS THE FINANCIAL-INCLUSION RAIL. It is delivered through Business Correspondents at micro-ATMs and supports cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar fund transfer, eKYC and best-finger detection.
6. LEARN THE CHARGES POSITION. The RBI waived its own processing and time-varying charges on RTGS and NEFT from 1 July 2019, and from 1 January 2020 directed banks not to levy charges on savings account holders for online NEFT transactions.
7. KEEP TWO CURRENT-AFFAIRS ITEMS READY. UPI is built on the IMPS infrastructure and was launched by NPCI in 2016. NPCI's proposed 30% market-share cap on third-party UPI application providers has been deferred to 31 December 2026, so it is live current affairs during this exam cycle.
tricks: Decode the acronym instead of memorising the behaviour. 'Gross' in RTGS means one-by-one with no netting, which is why it is instant; 'Net' in NEFT's deferred net settlement means pooled, which is why it is batched. An examiner asking 'which of these settles on a deferred net basis' is answerable from the expansion alone.

Fix the ownership with one sentence: 'The RBI runs the two that need an IFSC and a bank branch; NPCI runs everything you can do from a phone.' RTGS and NEFT are RBI; IMPS, UPI, AEPS are NPCI. This resolves the most commonly asked question type in a second.

Store RTGS separately from the limits ladder because it is the exception — it is the only system with a MINIMUM. Trying to remember 'RTGS = 2 lakh' as a ceiling is the single most reliable way to lose this mark; encode it as 'RTGS starts at 2 lakh'.

Link each system to its unique identifier and answer identifier questions without recalling anything else: MMID belongs to IMPS and nothing else; VPA belongs to UPI and nothing else; a biometric belongs to AEPS and nothing else; IFSC belongs to NEFT, RTGS and IMPS.

Memorise the batch count as '48 half-hourly batches, on the hour and the half hour'. Questions frequently ask for the number of NEFT settlement batches per day, and 48 follows immediately from 24 x 2 if you have stored the interval rather than the count.
traps: Believing RTGS has a maximum limit. The RBI prescribes a minimum of Rs 2 lakh per customer transaction and no upper ceiling; individual banks may set their own channel-wise caps, but that is a bank rule, not an RBI rule. Options offering 'Rs 10 lakh' or 'Rs 25 lakh' as the RTGS maximum are testing exactly this.

Believing NEFT has a minimum. It does not. The Rs 50,000 figure attached to NEFT applies only to CASH-BASED walk-in remittances, not to account-to-account transfers, and options exploit this by presenting Rs 50,000 as a general NEFT ceiling.

Describing NEFT as instantaneous. It is batch-settled; credit reaches the beneficiary within a defined window after the batch in which the instruction settles. A question contrasting 'real-time' with 'batch' is asking you to separate RTGS from NEFT.
Assigning UPI or IMPS to the RBI. Both are NPCI products. Equally, assigning RTGS to NPCI. The ownership split is asked directly and in 'which of the following is NOT operated by NPCI' form.
Saying AEPS requires a debit card or a PIN. It requires an Aadhaar number, the issuing bank's IIN and a biometric. Options mentioning a card, a PIN or a cheque are wrong by construction.

Quoting the UPI limit as a flat Rs 1 lakh. Rs 1 lakh is the default; specified categories including capital markets, insurance, education and healthcare permit up to Rs 5 lakh per transaction. A question naming one of those categories is testing the exception.
Confusing UPI Lite's two numbers. Rs 1,000 is the per-transaction cap; Rs 5,000 is the maximum balance the on-device wallet may hold. Both appear as options in the same question.

A statement-based 'which of the following is/are correct' question with three or four statements: 35-45 seconds. If a payments question takes you longer than 45 seconds, the fact is not memorised and no amount of thinking will produce it — mark it and move, since 0.25 is deducted for a wrong answer.

ga-accounts.topicName: Account Types — Savings, Current, FD, RD, NRI
ga-accounts.whatItIs: The deposit products a bank offers and the rules that distinguish them: who may open each, whether interest is paid, what restrictions apply, how the interest is taxed, and how much of the money is insured. It splits into three groups. DEMAND deposits — savings and current — are payable on demand. TERM deposits — fixed and recurring — are locked for a chosen period at a fixed rate. NRI deposits — NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) — are governed by FEMA and differ chiefly in currency, taxability and repatriability. Examiners ask this as pure recall, usually as a difference question ('which of the following is true of a current account') or a multi-statement question. Figures verified in 2026; the tax thresholds in particular should be re-checked before the Mains on 27 December 2026.
ga-accounts.coreMethod:
1. SAVINGS ACCOUNT. For individuals and certain non-trading entities; not for business or trading purposes. Interest is calculated on the DAILY closing balance (mandatory since 1 April 2010) and credited at quarterly or shorter intervals. The rate has been deregulated since October 2011, so each bank sets its own. Banks may restrict the number of free withdrawals and may require a minimum balance.
2. CURRENT ACCOUNT. For businesses, firms and companies. NO interest is payable. Unlimited transactions, overdraft facility available, cheque-book and other business services. The trade-off is simple: liquidity and volume instead of interest.
3. BSBDA (Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account). A zero-balance savings account that must be offered free of charge with no minimum balance requirement, a free RuPay ATM-cum-debit card, and a minimum of four withdrawals per month at no charge. A BSBDA holder may not hold any other savings account in the same bank. The related SMALL ACCOUNT, for people lacking officially valid KYC documents, is subject to a balance ceiling of Rs 50,000, annual credits of Rs 1 lakh, and monthly withdrawals of Rs 10,000, and is normally valid for 12 months, extendable.
4. FIXED DEPOSIT (FD). A lump sum locked for a chosen tenor, commonly from 7 days up to 10 years, at a rate fixed at the time of booking. Premature withdrawal usually attracts a penalty and a lower applicable rate. Loans or overdrafts are typically available against the deposit. A TAX-SAVER FD has a 5-year lock-in, qualifies for deduction under Section 80C up to Rs 1.5 lakh, and permits neither premature withdrawal nor a loan against it.
5. RECURRING DEPOSIT (RD). A fixed instalment paid every month for a chosen period, earning the same order of interest as an FD. It suits salaried savers building a corpus rather than deploying one.
6. TAX POSITION. Interest on FDs and RDs is fully taxable. Under Section 194A, banks deduct TDS at 10% once the interest paid in a financial year exceeds Rs 50,000 for a general depositor or Rs 1 lakh for a senior citizen (thresholds effective from FY 2025-26); the rate becomes 20% if PAN is not furnished. Form 15G (for those below 60) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) may be submitted to avoid deduction where total income is below the taxable limit. TDS is not deducted on savings account interest, though that interest is still taxable.
7. NRI ACCOUNTS — THREE, DISTINGUISHED BY CURRENCY, TAX AND REPATRIATION.
   - NRE (Non-Resident External): held in Indian rupees, funded from income earned ABROAD. Interest is exempt from Indian income tax. Principal and interest are fully repatriable. The depositor bears the rupee exchange-rate risk.
   - NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary): held in Indian rupees, for income earned IN India such as rent, dividends and pension. Interest is taxable in India. Repatriation is permitted up to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to tax compliance and the filing of Forms 15CA and 15CB.
   - FCNR(B) (Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Banks)): a TERM DEPOSIT ONLY, held in a permitted foreign currency, with a tenor of 1 year to 5 years. Interest is exempt from Indian income tax and the deposit is fully repatriable. Because it is denominated in foreign currency, the depositor carries no rupee exchange risk.
8. DEPOSIT INSURANCE. The DICGC insures deposits up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank, covering principal plus interest, aggregated across all branches of that bank for deposits held in the same right and capacity. Savings, current, fixed and recurring deposits are covered, as are NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) deposits held with an insured bank in India. Excluded are deposits of foreign governments, deposits of the Central and State Governments, inter-bank deposits, and any amount due on a deposit received outside India.
9. NOMINATION. Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, with the relevant provisions in force from 1 November 2025, a depositor may nominate up to FOUR persons for a deposit account or a locker, either successively (in order of priority) or simultaneously (with specified shares totalling 100%).
10. DORMANCY AND UNCLAIMED DEPOSITS. An account with no customer-induced transaction for two years is classified as inoperative. Deposits unclaimed for ten years are transferred to the RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund, and can be searched through the RBI's UDGAM portal.
tricks: Sort every account question by asking one question first: is this a DEMAND deposit or a TERM deposit? Savings and current are demand; FD and RD are term. Almost every 'which of the following' option about premature withdrawal, penalties or fixed tenors resolves the moment you place the product in the right bucket.

Fix the NRI trio with a three-word tag each: NRE is 'foreign money, rupee account, tax-free'; NRO is 'Indian money, rupee account, taxable'; FCNR(B) is 'foreign currency, term deposit only, tax-free'. Every NRI question in this exam is answerable from those three tags plus the USD 1 million NRO repatriation cap.

Remember that current accounts pay NO interest as a rule with no threshold attached to it. Options that offer '2% on current accounts' or 'interest above a balance of Rs 1 lakh' are wrong by construction, which lets you eliminate before reading the rest.

Store the two TDS thresholds as a pair — Rs 50,000 general and Rs 1 lakh senior citizen — because IBPS asks them together and the senior-citizen figure is exactly double. Attach '10% with PAN, 20% without' to the same card.

Encode the DICGC cover as 'Rs 5 lakh, per depositor, per bank, principal plus interest'. Each of those four phrases is separately tested: options will vary the amount, or say 'per account' instead of 'per depositor', or 'per branch' instead of 'per bank', or 'principal only'.
traps: Thinking DICGC cover is per account or per branch. It is per depositor per bank, with all branches of that bank aggregated. Someone with four accounts at one bank is covered to Rs 5 lakh in total, not Rs 20 lakh.
Thinking DICGC covers only the principal. It covers principal PLUS interest, subject to the Rs 5 lakh ceiling.
Assuming FCNR(B) can be a savings account. It is a TERM DEPOSIT ONLY, with a tenor of 1 to 5 years. NRE and NRO can each be savings, current, recurring or fixed; FCNR(B) cannot.

Swapping NRE and NRO on taxability. NRE interest is tax-free in India; NRO interest is taxable. The mnemonic that fails people is the one based on the letters, so anchor instead on the source of the money: money earned in India is taxed in India.
Believing the NRO repatriation limit is per calendar year or per transaction. It is USD 1 million per FINANCIAL YEAR, and it requires tax compliance with Forms 15CA and 15CB.

Applying the old TDS threshold of Rs 40,000. From FY 2025-26 it is Rs 50,000 for general depositors and Rs 1 lakh for senior citizens under Section 194A. Papers set after April 2025 test the revised figures.

Assuming a tax-saver FD behaves like an ordinary FD. It has a compulsory 5-year lock-in, cannot be broken prematurely, and no loan can be taken against it — the exact opposite of the ordinary FD's flexibility.

Stating that only one nominee is permitted per deposit account. Since 1 November 2025 up to four nominees are permitted, either successively or simultaneously — a change recent enough to be a live current-affairs question in this cycle.
Confusing the two-year dormancy trigger with the ten-year transfer to the DEA Fund. Two years makes an account inoperative; ten years sends the money to the DEA Fund.
